text:
incident-bot: [pager] High token-count delta detected for tenant pent-742 in VPC pool vpc-eu-02 (dedicated). Spike started ~1802509800. Alerts: billing-inflation, capacity-threshold. Paging oncall.

marta: oncall here, picking up. seeing a big jump in tokens per request for Pentarch. quick check: rate not changed, but median tokens/request jumped x6.

kyle: looking. any recent deploys to the tokenizer service in that VPC?

ash: no deploys from infra side. customer has a custom normalize hook in their private pipeline; could be related.

samir: logs snippet from the serving nodes (sanitized):
```
2026-07-12T14:02:01Z tenant=pent-742 pool=vpc-eu-02 request_id=rp_9a3 tokens_reported=2431 prompt_len=1024 model=gpt-small-2
2026-07-12T14:02:02Z tenant=pent-742 request_id=rp_9a4 tokens_reported=120 prompt_len=98 model=gpt-small-2
```
Pattern: same size prompts sometimes counted as 20x tokens.

marta: that looks like double-counting on some requests. Could be mismatch between the tokenizer library used by customer and the one we use to bill.

eduardo-support: customer (Pentarch) just posted in their support channel saying they saw bill spikes and throttling. They're on a strict reserved cap.

kyle: confirming: pent-742 is on dedicated pool with tenant isolation rules; we should avoid cross-tenant fallout. First priority: stop billing spike and mitigate capacity impact.

ash: ops note: we can toggle per-tenant rate limit to enforced-burst=0 to slow them and prevent queue pressure. Suggest doing that while we debug.

marta: do it. @ops-bot please apply temporary throttle: tenant pent-742 max-reqs-per-minute=30 and max-tokens-per-minute=10000. Please confirm when applied.

ops-bot: throttle applied to tenant pent-742: max-reqs-per-minute=30 max-tokens-per-minute=10000 (applied by @ops-bot at 1802510203).

samir: running a sample diff between our tokenizer and the customer's normalization output. Found edgecases: customers sometimes send legacy UTF-16 surrogates and a newline-delimited JSON array; their preprocessor expands escape sequences into literal backslashes causing different tokenization. Example: customer supplied string "\\u2019" got normalized into "\u2019" then raw-decoded by our tokenizer resulting in extra bytes.

kyle: can you paste a minimal repro? We can run a recount job and mark affected requests for credit.

samir: repro payload below (redacted):
```
{"user_input": "Price's latest report:\n  - revenue: $1.2M\n  - note: don\'t use smart quotes \u2019 in headers"}
```
Our preprocessor (server-side) sees the `\\u2019` and decodes to `\u2019` which then becomes the two-character sequence `\\` + `u` in the customer's pipeline, they count as separate tokens.

marta: TL;DR: mismatch in string unescaping between customer library and our billing/token-count path. That inflates tokens and triggers both billing and queue pressure.

ash: mitigation plan: 1) throttle (done) 2) add a temporary post-tokenization normalization step that collapses legacy escape expansions for this tenant before token counting 3) run a recount over last 3 hours to estimate overbilled tokens 4) notify support/cs for credits and customer comms 5) patch the billing pipeline to canonicalize escapes.

kyle: I'm on the hotfix for step 2 — will push a tenant-scoped normalization flag in the token-counter service and enable it for pent-742. Rolling to 2 nodes now, will monitor.

samir: while kyle rolls, I'll kick off a retrospective recount job with the tokenized payloads we stored for the tenant. Might need 30m-45m.

eduardo-support: I'll prepare a customer-facing note: "We've identified an encoding mismatch between our token counting and a custom preprocessor on your side that expands legacy escapes. We've paused automatic throttles and applied temporary rate-limits to protect your quota while we resolve. We will audit recent usage and issue credits if necessary." Want review before sending.

marta: keep it factual, avoid blame. Offer timeline and next steps. Also ask them to share a sample of their preprocessor or confirm they expanded escapes intentionally.

kyle: hotfix rolled to 2/2 token-count nodes (canary). Enabling tenant-scoped normalization flag for pent-742 now. Command used:
```
curl -X POST https://internal.token-counter/_flags -d '{"tenant":"pent-742","normalize_escapes":true}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>'
```
Enabling...

ops-bot: feature flag set for tenant pent-742 (normalize_escapes=true) at 1802510802 on nodes token-01, token-02.

kyle: early metrics: median tokens/request for pent-742 back to expected range after flag. Queue depth on vpc-eu-02 dropping.

marta: great. Samir, status on recount?

samir: recount job kicked. Preliminary estimate: ~18k inflated tokens in last 3 hours across ~220 requests. Will produce CSV of request ids and corrected counts.

eduardo-support: CS draft ready. Will wait for the CSV and proposed credit amount. We'll offer a one-time credit and a follow-up sync.

ash: ops note: leaving throttle in place for 2 hours to ensure full stabilization. We can relax sooner if telemetry stays green.

marta: @kyle please open a short-lived runbook entry and a postmortem ticket. Include: root cause (escape-decoding mismatch), mitigation (tenant flag), follow-ups (canonicalization in billing path, unit tests for escape sequences, add e2e test with customer's sample), customer comms + credit. Assign owners.

kyle: created ticket INF-6139 and assigned follow-ups: canonicalization -> samir, billing audit -> eduardo-support, test coverage -> ash.

eduardo-support: sending customer note now. I'll BCC account exec.

marta: handoff to day oncall in 45m. @kyle and @samir please add notes to the oncall doc. Any legal/compliance concern?

ash: nothing immediate but if customer wants logs with PII we'll route via compliance. Keep sanitized CSV for now.

incident-bot: incident status: mitigated -> partial (throttle + tenant flag applied). Next update scheduled in 30 minutes.

kyle: followup: pushing a small PR to the billing path to normalize escapes (will be code-reviewed). Link: https://phab.redwood/PR/7231 (internal).

samir: recount complete. CSV and proposed credit calculation uploaded to INF-6139. Estimate credit = $124.12 — rounding per billing policy.

eduardo-support: customer responded: thanks, appreciates quick response and asked for root-cause writeup. Scheduling 1:1 tomorrow.

marta: OK. leaving notes and closing pager. If anything resurfaces, re-pager. Good job team. :clap:

incident-bot: pager cleared at 1802512799.
